classification_definitions.integration: A real production service/API/network/process/store/filesystem boundary materially supports the core observable assertion.
classification_definitions.unit: Local validation/algorithm/control flow or fake provider/store assertions; incidental files are insufficient.
classification_definitions.mixed: Separate meaningful unit-only and real-boundary assertion blocks in one root.
classification_definitions.unresolved: Missing or contradictory connected source prevents resolving an assertion/category; distinct from runtime UNKNOWN.

roots.rationale: Bad manifest digest is rejected by the local pin comparison before PutObject. Zero writes is a fake map counter; fixture filesystem setup is incidental.
Conflicting selector preservation and five earlier writes are checked against the in-memory founderLedgerObjects map. There is no OCI HTTP or durable store boundary.

Fence errors, attempt advances and resumed launch count exercise control flow over a synthetic map ledger and OCI counters. Floor and signer reads are prerequisite authority setup, not the asserted mutation boundary.
HEAD failure is injected by rejectSuffix in the map store. Staged advance/restart and result readback use that same fake map and launch counter; real signer files are incidental.
Nil placement is a local checkAntiAffinity guard. No-launch is a fake counter; installed signer/floor files are unchanged prerequisites.

Matching replacement admission publishes the real local peer floor and accepted identity marker. The separate retired-instance rejection uses the fake physical observer/in-memory ledger identity mismatch before those publication effects and remains unit. No live OCI or credentials are qualified.
Attempt-two identity, create-key, summary, replay and stale evidence assertions read map-backed ledger state and fake OCI counters. Real signer-file reads are incidental authority setup.
Untrusted, cross-slot and seed-slot evidence checks are local authorization validation. Ledger state and no-launch assertions use the map/counter fakes.
ObserveLifecycle receives a fixed fake GetInstance response. TERMINATED, wrong returned ID and malformed-ID checks are local response validation, with no network or VNIC boundary.
Candidate-only recovery asserts synthetic launch/observation counts and map ledger result/candidate association. Real signer/floor prerequisites do not establish a real OCI or store boundary.
Synthetic stale facts and fake terminated instance drive rejection. Assertions observe fake launches, observations and map write counts; no actual instance observation boundary is reached.

Each case actually removes/corrupts a floor file or removes its lock. Production verifyExistingFounderFloor opens the real directory/lock and validates the real floor bytes before the completion callback. The filesystem trust boundary is the core target.

The separate ReadCurrent(now+2h) expiry error checks synthetic selector authority and remains unit. Completed seed restart crosses actual existing floor validation and the local completion-fact filesystem path, returning without consulting expired selector or OCI. Fake historical ledger itself is not integration.

Initial admission publishes a real peer floor and accepted identity marker; AdmitRestart reads the marker and installed trust files after the synthetic clock passes launch deadline. The separate founderPeersComplete assertion at lines976–979 inspects only map-backed ledger completion and remains unit. Those independent local and filesystem assertion blocks make this root mixed. OCI, ledger and material/credential clients remain fakes.
Both planned peers and repeated restarts are asserted only through fake OCI counters and in-memory ledger. Signer/floor reads are prerequisites, not the launch/restart observable.

Expired receipt from the map ledger is rejected by initialProofs before material/floor/marker publication. Fake counters and a negative marker absence read support this pre-publication guard; no successful durable publication/readback is established.

The wrapper invokes the actual InitializePeerForService floor write/fsync before advancing the fake clock. Gate must revalidate and reject, leaving no accepted marker as checked by production MarkerStore.ReadIdentity. Real floor publication is material to this after-publication expiry target; material/credential calls are counted fakes.
Wrong AcceptedInstall anchor digest is rejected during local historical-anchor verification/digest comparison, before opening the historical instance-principal ledger. Fixture files are incidental.

LastModified is directly changed in the fake map. Gate returns pending before material/floor/marker publication; zero fake calls and marker absence verify the guard. This is synthetic timestamp/quarantine validation, not committed provider persistence.

Fake GetObject advances synthetic Date across selection expiry. Fresh authorization rejects before mutation/launch; observations are map write and OCI counter stability. Signer/floor files are incidental prerequisites.

qualification_limits: founderLedgerObjects and founderSelectionObjects are maps. founderFakeOCI/fakeComputeObservation return SDK structs directly. None establishes OCI HTTP/network/durable-store qualification.

Real signer/floor prerequisites are incidental to synthetic ledger/OCI assertions. Floor corruption/provisioning and successful marker publication/restart reads are credited only where material to the asserted target.
Negative marker absence reads after guards do not establish successful durable publication/readback.
Local filesystem effects do not establish crash/power-loss durability or live provider/runtime/deployment acceptance. All safety obligations retained.
No source/repository/ledger/runtime/count/deletion/retirement/completion mutation or credit. Independent peer review required.
